title: You don’t struggle to love God…
paragraphs:
You don’t struggle to love God…
You struggle to let go of what you love more.
Because this is where it gets uncomfortable.

You sing “I surrender all”…
But there’s a part of you whispering,
“Not this.”

Not that relationship.
Not that hidden habit.
Not that version of you that nobody sees.

You can look devoted…
and still be divided.

You can raise your hands in worship…
while your heart is bowing somewhere else.

You can say “God first”…
but live like He’s competing for your attention.

That late-night compromise.
That private sin.
That pride dressed up as “I got this.”
You don’t need a preacher to expose it.
This is where shame creeps in.

It whispers,
“You’ll never fully give yourself to God.”
“You’ve already failed too many times.”
“You’re not that kind of Christian.”
“You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.” — Matthew 22:37

Not fragments.
Not percentages.
Not what’s convenient.
Because partial love creates double lives.

God is not asking for 100% of your love
because He needs it.

He’s asking because anything less
will slowly break you.
“No one can serve two masters…” — Matthew 6:24
You already know how that feels.

One part of you wants holiness.
Another part craves control.

One part longs for God.
Another part clings to sin.
And the war inside you is exhausting.

God never demanded 100% from you…
without first giving 100% to you.

He didn’t say,
“I’ll give you part of My life if you clean yourself up first.”
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
While you were still choosing other things over Him.

His blood.
His breath.
His body.

Because your failure is real—
but it is not final.
Some scholars interpret repentance simply as “turning around.”
Because behavior modification can’t save you.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us…” — 1 John 1:9
Not if you fix yourself first.
If you come into the light.

You are more sinful than you admit—
but more loved than you ever imagined.
And Jesus is the only bridge between those two truths.
Not scrolling to the next post to escape this moment.
What are you still holding back?

That thing you say,
“It’s not that bad.”

Because full love begins
where full honesty starts.
You don’t need to come perfect.

You’ll find a Savior who already knew…
and still chose the cross.

But because He already was—
for you.
“Jesus, I’m done giving You pieces. I confess what I’ve been hiding. I surrender what I’ve been protecting. Cleanse me. Change me. Be Lord over all of my life. Not part. All.”
